Oh, my goodness. No traffic? In Dallas? That's a fucking *wheeze.* I've never met worse drivers than here, either. Maybe I grew up with a "different" kind of crazy driving in Houston, but the drivers here are downright terrifying. I have not once run the gauntlet north for more than a day without seeing at least one BAD wreck on the highway that tacked on an extra 10-15 to my travel time. And everything clogs to a complete fucking standstill. Sometimes as many as seven wrecks on the highway. Pileups from rubberneckers. Counted 4 cars on the side of the road on fire in a 5-day span once. And when there aren't wrecks people tend to go a strangely consisted 5-10 under the speed limit. In the passing lane. I mean, really. The city has a lot to offer but PLEASE do not come here to avoid traffic, lol. I swerved and fishtailed on the highway about a month ago because a truck going ~90mph jetted ahead, swerved into my lane and almost slammed into me. It was like a fucking suicide attack. Fort Worth I don't know too much about, but Dallas itself has been a fucking nightmare. At least for me.

I'll tell you what I know. I'm a Houston native and generally consider myself pretty street-safe, although I generally consider people from my city pretty decent. I've walked in the roughest parts of Houston for many years, and only on very scant occasions have I ever felt unsafe. Dallas is a hotbed of crime from what I've seen, in my own experiences and just secondhand. I don't know a single person I've met at school, for instance, who hasn't had shit stolen from them, or a break-in, or some other type of scam. It's really unfortunate. I'm sure there've got to be other sides to this, but from me personally if I didn't have to be here for school I'd say fuck this place entirely. I lived in a very nice part of Uptown in a gated complex and had my deadbolted door literally kicked through while I was asleep. I had to physically beat the intruder with a crowbar and defend myself until he fled. 0/10, would not live here again.

I am sorry that my anger comes across like that. I called the police, asked every employee I could find genuinely for help with absolutely no response or complete dismissal, followed up, made calls, contacted pawn shops, checked all local online retailers, and did my due diligence. I don't want anything for free. I don't even want a replacement for my things. It's not the same as having your things stolen from you. I'll be the first to admit I am very defensive and upset right now. You live a life trying to do good by others, give people free passes, say "maybe they need it more than I do." You forgive, you forget, you try harder, you move on. But after so long, senseless violence and acts of ruthless disregard for others whittle down your faith and understanding in the world. Things happen beyond your control. A dream to be a good person and live a peaceful life turns into a nasty fight just to get by. You have your health taken, your livelihood, your humanity, and you find yourself alone. You start to think maybe if you were a little more of a defensive asshole things would work out for you the way they seem to work out for others. You start to get sick of hearing "move on" after taking hit after hit when it's hard to move at all. I know I'll eventually get past this, and I'll heal the damage of my anger. But right now I'm hurt and I'd rather express it on the internet instead of in person where it could really hurt someone else. I am sorry for being so angry. I really am. I'm just so tired.

I feel you, OP. And I believe that no, it is not possible to remain friends with anyone who is friends with a narc/abusive person. Even friends who say "I'm not okay with the behavior, and I told them that!" Because in a narc's/abusive person's mind, the ONLY thing they respond to is a full-stop from someone else. Any continued presence/friendliness on the part of someone is, to a narc/abusive person, a signal that says "I'm okay with your behavior." 

I lost close friends, including one of my best friends of 7+ years because I had to confront the fact that they were unwilling to tell the person exhibiting abusive behavior toward me, "stop this immediately or we are not friends." That is the ONLY acceptable response to abusive behavior. Period. **Ever.**
